voice: Colin, first person. No business name, no cash claims, no number from our side, no promises on closing dates or tenants.

gate_legend.note: gate_item is a list; [] means the item settles identity only. Scores are 0-2 each, 12 points, scored after the call.

before_pickup: Property: address, municipality, type, units, year built, owner lives there?
Owner of record: names, owner type, mailing address, owned since (date only), other parcels
Why they might sell: tax years, sheriff sale date, code/raze cases, death or estate filing, vacancy (years only, no amounts)
What they said: their texts verbatim; reason, clock, who signs, their number (their words, never ours), flags; which text they are answering and when it went
Hard stops known: STOP/hostile on any phone; listed; signed elsewhere; sheriff sale inside 14 days; elderly/ill with no family named; estate with nobody who can sign
Gate box: six blank __/2 lines, filled after the call
Rules: never a number, range, percentage or value; never a company name; never a closing date, tenant removal or what I will do with the house; never re-ask a number they already gave

questions.say: Thanks for calling me back. Which place is this about, the one on {street}?
questions.listen_for: The address matches the card. A different address is a new property: ask whose name it is in. Unknown number: ask the address first.

questions.say: And is it your place, {first_name}, or are you helping someone with it?
questions.listen_for: Owner, spouse, adult child, tenant, manager, agent, wholesaler. Anyone but an owner or named family changes the call. Title is checked in records, not asked.
questions.branch: tenant -> reassure, no landlord plans discussed; agent -> stay out of the way, ask the listing end date; wholesaler -> polite exit; relative -> ask whether the owner would want to hear about it and how to reach them

questions.say: So what's the story over there? What's got you thinking about selling now?
questions.listen_for: Silence after asking. A need (move, money, tenant, death, behind) rather than a want; whether they connect it to selling. 'If the price is right' with nothing behind it is not a lead.
questions.branch: asked why I want to know -> 'I ask everyone, so I don't waste your time with a number that was never going to work.'

questions.say: Tell me a little about the place.
questions.listen_for: Specific defects in their own words are the clearest sign of a real seller. Vague 'needs some work' is a 1. A perfect house: loop back to the reason.
questions.branch: perfect house -> 'Sounds like a great place. Why would you even think about selling it?'

questions.say: Who's living there right now, you, a tenant, or is it sitting empty?
questions.listen_for: Owner / tenant / vacant; access for a visit. Only if not already said.

questions.say: If you listed it tomorrow, what would you have to do to it first?
questions.listen_for: Their own list of work. Only if not already said.

questions.say: Anything ever happen to it, like a leak or a fire?
questions.listen_for: A fire, water, foundation, a raze or code order. Only if not already said.

questions.say: If I bought it, where would you be headed, and when?
questions.listen_for: A concrete plan (sister's house, lease start, closing on the next place, court date) vs 'haven't thought about it'. Inside about 90 days gets full attention. A date with nothing behind it is a brush-off: ask what happens on that date.

questions.say: Is it just you on this, or is there anyone else who'd want to look at an offer before you said yes?
questions.listen_for: Spouse, siblings, heir, partner, 'my kids handle it'. Get the name and whether they can be on the next call or at the visit.
questions.branch: estate -> 'Are you the one handling the house for the family, and have the court papers come through yet?'; company -> who signs for it

questions.say: What do you need to get out of it to move on?
questions.listen_for: A figure, a refusal, or 'make me an offer'. Never 'asking price', 'what would you like' or 'lowest you'd take'. At most two asks on the whole call; a second refusal is the answer: write 'refused after two asks'.
questions.branch: 'what do you mean?' -> 'The number that makes it worth selling to you.'; 'make me an offer' -> objection obj_give_me_a_number

questions.say: How did you come up with that?
questions.listen_for: Silence after asking. Need (payoff, arrears, what they paid, the next place) vs market (Zillow, bank estimate, neighbour's sale, refused offers). Never argue the comps on the phone.

questions.say: I buy as-is and cover the repairs and the selling costs, so where I come in usually lands under what a listed sale would bring. If I came in under yours, would you still want to hear it?
questions.listen_for: Moved / open / depends / terms only / firm. A firm floor resting on a real need (payoff plus arrears) is a 1, not a 0.

questions.say: Do you owe anything on it? Roughly what's left is fine.
questions.listen_for: Only once a number is on the table or the records show distress. Payoff near or above their number: special review. 'Don't know' is fine; never interrogate.

questions.say: Are you behind on anything, the payment or the taxes?
questions.listen_for: A sale date. Inside 14 days is a hard stop: say honestly there isn't time for a sale, mention a free HUD housing counselor.
questions.branch: sale date inside 14 days -> hard stop, no walk

questions.say: Here's how I work. I'll come see it once, I'll have a straight number for you before I leave, and I'll tell you honestly if I can't get there. Before I come out: if the number works for both of us, are you in a spot to say yes or no on it, with everyone who'd need to sign there?
questions.listen_for: A plain yes; 'talk to my wife' (get her to the visit); 'think about it' (fine, ask what they'd want to think through). No guilt, no fake busyness, no market fear.
questions.branch: yes -> booking; not ready -> not_ready close

booking.say: When's a good time for me to come by and see it?
booking.note: One open question; it is also the test. A motivated owner names a time; a tire-kicker keeps asking for the number.

booking.say: Tomorrow afternoon, or would the weekend suit better?
booking.note: Only if they hesitate. Book inside 48 hours, not across a weekend where possible.

booking.say: Who'll let me in, you or a tenant? I'll work around your tenant; nobody has to move out for a sale.
Will {signer} be there? I'd rather hear everyone's questions at once than relay them.
booking.note: Everyone who would sign present or agreed. The most critical phone question.

booking.say: Is this the best number? If I don't pick up, text me; same for me.
booking.note: Best number and the text-if-no-answer rule.

booking.say: It takes about forty-five minutes. I'll walk it, ask a few things, and give you a straight number before I leave. Either way I'll tell you what I'd suggest in your shoes.
booking.note: Length, what happens, that a number comes before leaving.

booking.say: I'll text you the morning of to confirm.
booking.note: The app sends the morning-of reminder (cadence spec 3.4).

booking.say: Let me look everything over and call you back {day}. What time of day is best?
booking.note: When a visit is not warranted yet: no reason, a far number, a missing signer, or a desk check first. Honour the time exactly.

objections.trigger: Who are you / what company?
objections.say: It's just me, Colin Merrill. I buy houses around here myself and I'm looking for a couple more.
objections.note: No company name; no 'my partner'.

objections.trigger: Are you a wholesaler / do you buy it yourself?
objections.say: I'm the one buying it. I'll walk you through exactly how I buy when I see it.
objections.note: Final wording pending Colin's answer on whether he ever assigns (qualification logic c.12). Never 'never say wholesaler'.

objections.trigger: How did you get my number?
objections.say: The address is public record. The phone number came from a data provider I subscribe to.
objections.note: Never a marketing-department cover.

objections.trigger: Is this a scam?
objections.say: Fair question. Look me up: Colin Merrill, Milwaukee. I'll meet you anywhere you like, and I'll show ID at the door.
objections.note: Only what is true.

objections.trigger: Just give me a number / what's your offer?
objections.say: I can't put a real number on a place I haven't seen; it'd be like buying a car without a test drive, and a guess would just waste your time. Mind if I ask a few quick questions, then come see it?
objections.note: If they push: q7_number. Never a number, range or percentage.

objections.trigger: Are you going to lowball me?
objections.say: I won't be the highest number you could ever get; I'll be a straight one, as-is, with nothing to fix and no showings. If you need the most money, an agent is the better route.
objections.note: Best offer, not highest.

objections.trigger: I want retail / Zillow says X
objections.say: That's fair, and if the most money is what matters, listing it is probably your better route. What I'm good for is speed, certainty and taking it as it sits. If that ever matters more, keep this number.
objections.note: No Zillow digs, no net-proceeds arithmetic.

objections.trigger: I have an agent / it's listed
objections.say: Then I'll stay out of your agent's way. When does the agreement run through? If it ends without a sale, mind if I check in then?
objections.note: Hard stop for a walk. Date becomes a follow-up.

objections.trigger: I'll think about it
objections.say: Of course. What's the part you'd want to think through? Sometimes it's something I can just answer.
objections.note: Silence after. If nothing: 'Take your time. When should I check back, or would you rather reach out?' No guilt, no swing-by, no sitting in the car.

objections.trigger: I need to talk to my wife / husband / kids
objections.say: Totally fair. When are you two together next? I'll call then, or come by then, so you don't have to relay it.
objections.note: No 'is it because the number's low?', no calling the bluff.

objections.trigger: Send me an offer by text / email
objections.say: I'd be guessing, and a guess would only cost you. Let me come see it, and you'll have a straight number before I leave.
objections.note: If they refuse any visit: desk check and a call back; no written number.

objections.trigger: I already have another offer
objections.say: Good, you have options. Why haven't you taken it? I won't bid against them by phone. If it comes through, great; if it falls apart, would you want me as your backup?
objections.note: Ask once whether anything is signed. Signed: hard stop. No running the other buyer down.

objections.trigger: My house is in good shape, why would I sell cheap?
objections.say: You might not. Plenty of nice houses sell to me because of the timing, not the condition. What's got you thinking about it at all?
objections.note: Perfect house plus retail ask is a follow-up, not a visit.

objections.trigger: I'm not in a hurry / don't need to sell
objections.say: Understood, no pressure here. Before my text, were you thinking about selling at all?
objections.note: If no: 'Then I won't take your time. Do you own anything else you'd ever consider selling?' One exit question only.

objections.trigger: What do you do with the houses?
objections.say: Depends on the house. Some I fix and rent, some I fix and sell. I'll tell you which when I've seen it.
objections.note: Only true statements.

objections.trigger: Are you a real person?
objections.say: Yes, it's Colin, same guy who texted you. An automated assistant helps me with texts and notes; anything that matters, I handle myself.
objections.note: On a live call this is simply true.

objections.trigger: We're behind on payments / there's a sale date
objections.say: Thank you for telling me. What's the date? Nobody chooses not to pay; what happened?
objections.note: Inside 14 days: 'I'll be honest, there isn't time for me to help with a sale. A HUD housing counselor is free and can sometimes slow it down.' No fear close.

objections.trigger: The house is in probate / my mother passed
objections.say: I'm sorry about your mother. Are you the one handling the house for the family, and have the court papers come through yet? There's no hurry on my end.
objections.note: Condolence once. Elderly owner: the deal is with the family and their attorney, never the owner alone.

objections.trigger: I'm just curious what it's worth
objections.say: I'm not the right source for a value; I'm a buyer, not an appraiser, and I only price a place after I've seen it. Is selling something you're actually weighing, or just curious?
objections.note: Curious only: polite exit.

objections.trigger: I'm busy, call me later
objections.say: No problem. What day and time, and is this the best number? I'll text my name so you know it's me.
objections.note: Honour the time exactly; no extra questions.

objections.trigger: Stop calling / take me off
objections.say: Done. You won't hear from me again. Sorry to have bothered you.
objections.note: STOP everywhere, every phone, forever.

objections.trigger: A flat no
objections.say: No problem. Is that no to me, or no to ever selling?
objections.note: One ask, then let go.

not_ready.say: That's fine, and I'd rather you take your time than feel pushed. What would need to happen for selling to make sense, and roughly when?
not_ready.note: Listen for an event, not just a date.

not_ready.say: Mind if I check back around then? And if anything changes before that, this number reaches me; text if I don't pick up.
not_ready.note: Date goes in exactly as said, with the event. Never call before it.

not_ready.say: Understood. I'll leave it with you, then. Keep this number.
not_ready.note: No check-back set; Dead unless a public record changes.

not_ready.say: If convenience ever matters more than the last dollar, keep this number.
If that buyer isn't ready when it comes to it, I am. Call me if anything changes.

after_call.what: Reason in their words, with the date it was said
The date and the event behind it, or 'none'
Names, relationship, whether each can be at the visit
Their number exactly as said or 'refused after two asks'; need / market / mixed
moved / open / depends / terms only / firm; whether the floor rests on a need
Occupancy, the defects they named, access, anything that happened to it
Ballpark owed, behind on anything, any sale date
elderly or ill, grief, capacity concern, listed, signed elsewhere, family said no
Date, channel, who, and the one thing to reference
visit booked / call back at time / not now with date / not now no date / no / STOP / wrong person
Rapport notes in their words: family, occupation, what they care about
Six items, 0-2 each, filled after the call
